note: The worker does an atomic set-if-absent on the auxiliary Redis (SET B_C 1 NX); only when the key was newly created does it add the sender to the main Redis set.
checker_note: As described ('check if the entry exists, then write'), two workers handling messages from the same sender can both see 'missing' and both write. Redis can do the check and the write atomically: SET key value NX only sets the key if it does not already exist and returns OK when it set it (nil otherwise), so the worker writes to the main Redis only on OK. Adding EX gives the key a TTL. Duplicates are harmless here (SADD is idempotent), so this is a precision point.

additions.text: Redis can do the auxiliary 'check and set' in one atomic command: SET key value NX sets the key only if it does not exist and returns OK when it did (nil otherwise). Adding EX seconds gives the key a TTL, so stale entries eventually disappear.

note: The auxiliary store can keep per-pair existence flags; storing them as fields of one hash per user (HSETNX) keeps the check O(1) and makes clearing a single delete.
checker_note: Separate per-pair keys (B_C: true) make the clear path harder than the lecture suggests: Redis cannot delete keys by prefix without KEYS (documented as dangerous in production) or SCAN, so the clear API must know every sender (e.g. read the main set first). In Redis Cluster B_C and B_D also hash to different slots unless a hash tag such as {B} is used. One hash per user (key B, field C, HSETNX) keeps existence checks O(1) and lets a single DEL clear everything.

additions.text: An alternative to one key per (receiver, sender) pair is one hash per receiver: HSETNX B C 1 sets field C only if it is absent and returns 1 if it did. A single DEL B clears the user, and since Redis 7.4 HEXPIRE can give individual fields a TTL.

note: If the two writes get out of sync the badge can under-count, possibly until the next clear; writing the main store first and giving auxiliary keys a TTL limits this.
checker_note: The worst case depends on write order and can be persistent, not only a lower count. If the auxiliary key is written but the main-Redis write fails, every later message from that sender is skipped and the sender never appears until the next clear. If clear deletes the main set but the auxiliary delete fails, new messages from those senders are suppressed and the badge can stay at 0. Writing the main Redis first and then the auxiliary key (a failure then only causes a harmless duplicate SADD), plus a TTL on auxiliary keys (SET ... NX EX), bounds the damage.
